archetype: A mono-red critical-mass copy engine wearing an aggro costume. deck-audit matches it to `aggro` from strategic_frame.json and the creature count agrees (27, inside 26-32), but the frame's reading is the right one: the 1/1s are not the clock, they are Zada's copy multiplier, Skirk Prospector's mana and Skullclamp's fuel. Two half-decks share the 99 — a commander-gated copy engine and a storm half that never touches the command zone — and only the first is gated.
verdict: This deck functions and it builds: the mana base is at every target, the turn-3 land drop lands 90% of the time, and five stacks are checker-passed. Read the gating before the prescription. Of the three declared targets only `Zada online with a cantrip drawn` is `commander_gated: true`; `Early token maker drawn` and `Storm payoff plus ritual drawn` are both false. Of the five passing stacks only 001 and 003 put Zada on the board — 002 resolves off Impact Tremors and four Mountains, 005 off Storm-Kiln Artist and three tokens, and 004 states in its own extras that she is in the command zone. So the storm half, including the Storm-Kiln Artist + Haze of Rage line that drives the bracket-4 floor, does not need her. What is limited is the half that carries the deck: the 66.1%-assembling plan and the only checker-passed kill (003) both need one 3/3 to survive the turn you commit, and the deck holds exactly one card that helps — Swiftfoot Boots, since Roaming Throne's Ward {2} is on Roaming Throne.

components.reading: The one-target enabler class and the thinnest component of the only commander-gated target: 6 cards, 36.4% of opening sevens, 44.4% by turn three. The redundancy table puts 6 between 31% and 41%; ten would buy 54%.

Five early body-makers, 31.2% of openers, drawn by mean turn 3.184 in 60% of runs. The deck has plenty of later bodies; what is thin is bodies BEFORE the pivot, and mean bodies on turn 4 is 2.698. This component feeds both halves.

Two cards, 13.7% of opening sevens — the thinnest group in the declared engine, and why the storm target assembles in 15.2% of runs (9.1% by turn 6). Stack 002 shows what it does when it lands: 8 damage to each opponent, not a kill.
The ritual half of the storm target, 25.8% of openers. Not the binding half — the payoff group is half its size.
Undeclared by goldfish_targets.json and therefore never simulated. One card in 99 keeps the hub alive; the audit's count of 2 includes Roaming Throne, whose Ward {2} is on itself.

The deck's only checker-verified infinite (stack 005) and the driver of its bracket-4 floor, and it needs no commander — its scenario board is Storm-Kiln Artist and three tokens. single_points_of_failure.why: Scope first: one of three declared targets is `commander_gated: true` and two of five passing stacks hold her on the board, so this is a single point of failure for the deck's best plan, not for the deck. Inside that scope it is sharp — 003 is the only checker-passed kill and it needs her, and the correct play makes exposure worse, since mean bodies rises from 2.698 on turn 4 to 5.257 by turn 6 and the pilot is rewarded for waiting. Swiftfoot Boots is the only card in the 99 that answers that. Lightning Greaves is a partial answer rather than a trap: its shroud does stop your own cantrip from targeting her, but equip is {0}, so on your own main phase you move it off for free before casting; what it cannot do is protect her during the pivot turn itself, which is exactly when you telegraph.

open_questions.question: Does the verified Storm-Kiln Artist + Haze of Rage loop convert into a kill — cast Grapeshot off the infinite storm count, or attack with the arbitrarily-pumped team?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 005's own final state records both opponents 'unaffected', so the deck's flagship line and bracket-4 driver is a verified engine with no verified kill attached. This is the single largest thing separating threat-density from a strength.

open_questions.question: Cast Daring Discovery targeting only Zada: does her trigger copy it for each other creature, and does each copy's Discover 4 resolve?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Daring Discovery has no entry in `card_roles.json` and is counted by no axis. If the copies each Discover it is quietly the deck's largest card-advantage burst; if not, it is a five-mana sorcery in a modal-2 deck and the next cut.

open_questions.why_it_matters: strategic_frame.json already queues this. It decides whether Roaming Throne is a four-mana doubler of the deck's best effect or a 4/4 body whose Ward {2} the protection axis is miscounting as commander insurance.

open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only pool line that both deepens the thinnest gated component and would add a second verified kill; without a passing stack the add rests on the redundancy argument alone.

gaps: No `deck_recon.json` exists for this deck, so nothing here is grounded in what strong Zada lists actually run — there are no per-commander inclusion rates in any artifact in this repo. Every add is argued from this deck's own measurements. Settled by a `deck-recon` pass.

Goldfish models resource development only — no removal, no interaction. Nothing measures how often Zada actually survives to the pivot turn, so the protection finding is an argument from card counts, gating flags and the corpus, not a simulated rate.

`Chaos Warp` has no entry in `card_roles.json`, so the deck's only catch-all answer is invisible to `interaction` and `interaction-breadth`. Same class of miss: `Daring Discovery`, `Spreading Insurrection`, `Fists of Flame` and `Wild Ride` are all unclassified.

strategic_frame.json lists 'No storm/critical-mass theory section' and 'No commander-protection/insurance section' among its gaps. Both now exist — `strategy:critical-mass.storm-math` and `strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance` — and are cited here, so the frame's gap list is stale on those two entries.

The corpus has no section on a commander whose own ability requires you to target it. `strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance` recommends boots-style constant protection without that caveat, and the Lightning Greaves reading here — shroud blocks your own cantrip, but equip {0} lets you move it off on your main phase, so the real cost is only during the pivot turn — is read off the cards, not cited. Settled by a `research-strategy` pass.

The bench holds one card (Sazacap's Brew) and strategic_frame.json records why it is not a Zada enabler: it targets a player, so the copy trigger never fires. There is effectively no sideboard to draw on.
